setup: The baker took out a huge loan to expand his sourdough business.
punchline: Now he kneads every extra cent just to stay afloat.
text: The baker took out a huge loan to expand his sourdough business. Now he kneads every extra cent just to stay afloat.
notes: Pun: 'kneads' plays on 'needs', reframing baking labor as financial desperation.

setup: The detective stared at the empty vault for a full minute before speaking.
punchline: He asked if anyone remembered where he parked his car.
text: The detective stared at the empty vault for a full minute before speaking. He asked if anyone remembered where he parked his car.
notes: Misdirection: builds expectation of forensic insight, subverts with mundane personal distraction.

setup: The new manager told the interns to really think outside the box.
punchline: So they held the entire meeting standing in the parking lot.
text: The new manager told the interns to really think outside the box. So they held the entire meeting standing in the parking lot.
notes: Literalized idiom: 'think outside the box' is enacted literally as standing outside the building.

setup: My grandmother said she'd never once missed a Sunday at church in sixty years.
punchline: Turns out she's been the one dusting the pews since 1974.
text: My grandmother said she'd never once missed a Sunday at church in sixty years. Turns out she's been the one dusting the pews since 1974.
notes: Reframe: 'never missed church' shifts from worshipper attendance to caretaker's unpaid labor.

setup: The marathon runner trained every single day for two years before the race.
punchline: On race morning, he overslept and missed the start entirely.
text: The marathon runner trained every single day for two years before the race. On race morning, he overslept and missed the start entirely.
notes: Inferable twist: heavy setup on dedication telegraphs an ironic reversal of effort.

setup: The magician promised the audience an ending nobody would ever forget.
punchline: He forgot his own final trick halfway through.
text: The magician promised the audience an ending nobody would ever forget. He forgot his own final trick halfway through.
notes: Inferable twist: a promise of an unforgettable ending telegraphs the promiser's own failure.

setup: A guy walks into a bar and orders the strangest drink on the menu.
punchline: The bus route downtown was rerouted due to construction this week.
text: A guy walks into a bar and orders the strangest drink on the menu. The bus route downtown was rerouted due to construction this week.
notes: Classic joke opener followed by an unrelated, plainly fluent civic sentence; no wordplay or link.

setup: My dog refuses to eat anything that isn't perfectly round.
punchline: The library extended its hours during final exam season.
text: My dog refuses to eat anything that isn't perfectly round. The library extended its hours during final exam season.
notes: Whimsical setup expecting a punchline, resolved instead by an unconnected mundane fact.

setup: The waiter brought out a cake with way too many candles on it.
punchline: Property taxes in the county increased slightly this year.
text: The waiter brought out a cake with way too many candles on it. Property taxes in the county increased slightly this year.
notes: Comedic birthday setup abandoned for a flat, unrelated statement about taxes.

setup: Two coworkers got stuck in the elevator for almost an hour.
punchline: The farmer's market moves indoors once the weather turns cold.
text: Two coworkers got stuck in the elevator for almost an hour. The farmer's market moves indoors once the weather turns cold.
notes: Sitcom-ready premise followed by an unconnected seasonal logistics sentence.

setup: She tried to parallel park for the fourth time in front of everyone.
punchline: The recipe calls for two cups of flour and a pinch of salt.
text: She tried to parallel park for the fourth time in front of everyone. The recipe calls for two cups of flour and a pinch of salt.
notes: Embarrassment setup swapped for an unrelated, plain baking instruction.

setup: The toddler insisted on wearing his superhero cape to the dentist.
punchline: The train schedule changes on weekends and public holidays.
text: The toddler insisted on wearing his superhero cape to the dentist. The train schedule changes on weekends and public holidays.
notes: Cute anecdotal setup dropped for a flat, unrelated transit fact.

setup: He plugged in the toaster and pressed the lever down.
punchline: A few minutes later, his toast popped up nicely browned.
text: He plugged in the toaster and pressed the lever down. A few minutes later, his toast popped up nicely browned.
notes: Mundane appliance action followed by the exact outcome anyone would predict.

setup: She set her alarm for seven in the morning before going to bed.
punchline: It rang at seven and woke her up right on time.
text: She set her alarm for seven in the morning before going to bed. It rang at seven and woke her up right on time.
notes: Routine setup resolved with the fully expected, unsurprising result.

setup: The waiter took their order and walked it back to the kitchen.
punchline: The chef began preparing the meal as soon as he got it.
text: The waiter took their order and walked it back to the kitchen. The chef began preparing the meal as soon as he got it.
notes: Ordinary restaurant sequence continued with its obvious, expected next step.

setup: The old fisherman untangled his net for the third time that morning.
punchline: Some things in life simply are what they are, in the end.
text: The old fisherman untangled his net for the third time that morning. Some things in life simply are what they are, in the end.
notes: Concrete labor scene capped with a portentous truism that resolves nothing about the scene.

setup: She found her father's watch in a drawer while cleaning out the house.
punchline: Time moves through us all in ways we can never fully grasp.
text: She found her father's watch in a drawer while cleaning out the house. Time moves through us all in ways we can never fully grasp.
notes: Concrete grief-adjacent detail followed by vague gesturing at profundity with no specific payoff.

setup: The construction crew paused when the crane made a strange grinding sound.
punchline: Everything, in some sense, is always building toward something else.
text: The construction crew paused when the crane made a strange grinding sound. Everything, in some sense, is always building toward something else.
notes: Concrete mechanical incident capped with a vague, unresolved abstraction gesturing at meaning.
